key_insight: Elastic turbulence gains broadband spectra from polymer-stress sheets that amplify as they thin, rather than from a hierarchy of inertial eddies.
engineering_relevance: This geometric mechanism could guide modeling of low-inertia polymer flows where elastic stresses generate complex motion despite spatially smooth velocities.
method: Identify elastic frontogenesis: in-plane stretching and cross-sheet compression concentrate polymer stress.
Relate sheet geometry and amplification during thinning to the polymer conformation spectrum.
Use the Stokes response to connect stress scaling to the velocity spectrum.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust power-law spectra in velocity and polymer conformation, but provides no numerical exponents, datasets, or evaluation details.
watch_item: The proposed model-independent mechanism still requires validation across constitutive models and operating regimes.
paper_title: Elastic frontogenesis sets the spectra of smooth elastic turbulence
